name: Alawa
catalog_quote: In the phonological phrase the basic stress pattern is that of a rapid build up of intensity on the first syllable, and a decay of intensity on the last one to three syllables ... Within words, the penultimate syllable tends to have slightly more stress, and within the phrase marked stress is heard on certain words, usually grammatically predictable.

audit.recode_to: Probably fixed-dominant (penult, stem domain) rather than fixed-strict, pending a full read of Sharpe 1972 pp.34-35: her own text (confirmed in snippets) says word stress is weak and often obscured by phrase stress, is heard on the penult 'of the stem' with variation, that 4-syllable stems carry stresses on 1st and 3rd with the primary hard to pick, and that reduplicated stems are an exception; the sweep's own read_rule note records 3-syllable stems 'a large number heard as having stress initial' and 5-syllable stems penult or antepenult with initial secondary. 'Strict penult at all lengths, no secondary' overstates this.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: no held file for Sharpe 1972; held items are readers and comparative papers with zero stress content. Google Books snippets fetched sources now confirm the p.14 'rapid build up of intensity...' clause and the p.34-35 core sentences verbatim, but not the p.14 'Within words, the penultimate syllable tends to have slightly more stress' clause; the sweep's continuous read came from dokumen.pub, which is off-limits, so the record is effectively snippet-grade while its grade field is blank and 'ver' claims a source check. (2) Deciding source: Sharpe 1972 is a reference grammar with dedicated word- and phrase-stress sections and instrumental (Mingograph) backing; Glottolog lists nothing better (the other refs are the same work as a thesis, a voice-quality paper I fetched sources and found silent on stress, and morphology papers); web search found no later phonology/prosody study or JIPA illust
audit.second_reader_evidence: Quote check. Confirmed: we hold no copy of Sharpe 1972 (AIAS AAS 37); the held morphstress_f2 files (Alawa readers, Capell 1979, Merlan 2003, thesis abstract) contain no stress statement (grep stress/penult: 0 relevant hits), and the Sharpe 1970 PL C-13 paper the first first reader fetched sources is silent on stress (pp.125-127 are articulatory setting only; I re-read the text layer). The sweep row (audit422/full_sweep/, 'Alawa') did take pp.13-15 from a shadow-library preview plus Google Books snippets, and the record's grade field is blank while 'ver' claims a source check.
